# Pull Request
Usage: https://meilisearch.notion.site/Dumpless-upgrade-fff4b06b651f81f1acafe24d4687b3f7?pvs=74

## Related issue
Fixes https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/5162

## What does this PR do?
- Implement the dumpless upgrade with multiple hooks:
  - In meilisearch directly before the task queue has been opened
  - In the index-scheduler while processing the task
  - In milli while upgrading the indexes
- There is no hook at search/query time to handle the old version of a database. That's left to the next person upgrading a database
- A new special type of task (`upgradeDatabase`) that can be retried has been introduced
- A new experimental cli flag has been introduced
- The version has been upgraded to the v1.13.0 in this PR otherwise it was a lot of useless work to test the dumpless upgrade
- Multiple tests have been introduced

## PR checklist
Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:
- [ ] Update the issue template we use for features, mentioning what we should do in case of a database upgrade
- [x] The experimental feature discussion should be opened and updated in the PR
- [x] Update the PRD
    - [x] Add the new error codes => No new error code since it's an internal error when it fails
    - [x] Add the task details
    - [x] Add the telemetry

## Notes

The new tests introduced are not _that_ slow

comments:
This would be a great addition. :)

On MySQL you have an option to auto upgrade (also on minor upgrades), but on PostgreSQL you haven't. 

It's no excuse not to make snapshots of your databases, but sometimes it isn't that important (like you can sync it manually later, e.g. Laravel Scout) and creating dumps of static data, isn't something you want to do on a daily basis.

does that work with just disconnected instead of the timeout?
I checked, and no, since the index-scheduler receiver channel has not been dropped it can still answer with `Timeout` :pensive:

a way for the test not to be flaky and have unprocessed task would be to test the case of a failing upgrade.

Properties to check:

1. After the upgrade task fails, no task is ever processed
2. The VERSION file has been rewritten
3. After the upgrade task fails, it is still possible to enqueue new tasks
4. Restarting the server after the task failed restart the task and attempts it again

- Testing (1), (2), (3) can be done by doctoring a data.ms to contain e.g. an index with the wrong version that will cause the upgrade to fail.
- Testing (4) can be done by doctoring a data.ms to contain a failed upgrade task (for example, as in the previous bullet point), then doctoring again such that the task will pass (for example, by removing the wrong version in the faulty index)
The early exit won't work for batches containing a single task. Please handle this case separately
